checks.title: Storage bucket is publicly accessible
checks.remediation: Block public access at the bucket and account level, and share data through signed URLs or authenticated access instead.

checks.title: Storage bucket is not encrypted at rest
checks.remediation: Enable default encryption on the bucket, preferably with a customer-managed key.

checks.title: Storage bucket access logging is off
checks.remediation: Turn on server access logging and send the logs to a separate, restricted bucket.

checks.title: Versioning is off on a bucket holding sensitive data
checks.remediation: Enable versioning so deleted or overwritten objects, including those hit by ransomware, can be recovered.

checks.title: Remote administration ports open to the internet
checks.remediation: Remove 0.0.0.0/0 rules for SSH, RDP, VNC, and Telnet; use a bastion host, VPN, or session manager service instead.

checks.title: All ports open to the internet
checks.remediation: Replace the all-ports rule with rules for only the ports and sources the workload needs.

checks.title: Load balancer allows plaintext HTTP or TLS below 1.2
checks.remediation: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS and apply a TLS policy that allows only TLS 1.2 or 1.3 with FIPS-validated ciphers.

checks.title: Server disk is not encrypted
checks.remediation: Encrypt the volume (snapshot, copy encrypted, and replace) and turn on encryption by default for new volumes.

checks.title: Server is not covered by patching and vulnerability scanning
checks.remediation: Install the patch management and scanning agent so the server is patched and scanned on schedule.

checks.title: Database is publicly accessible
checks.remediation: Disable public accessibility and place the database in private subnets reachable only from application servers.

checks.title: Database is not encrypted at rest
checks.remediation: Enable storage encryption; for existing databases, restore an encrypted copy from a snapshot.

checks.title: Database backups are off or kept too briefly
checks.remediation: Enable automated backups with a retention period that meets your recovery requirements.

checks.title: Root or global administrator account without MFA
checks.remediation: Protect the root account with a hardware security key and store recovery details securely.

checks.title: Root account has access keys
checks.remediation: Delete root access keys; use individual roles with least privilege for automation.

checks.title: Console user without MFA
checks.remediation: Require MFA for every console user, ideally through single sign-on with phishing-resistant MFA.

checks.title: Access keys older than the rotation period
checks.remediation: Rotate the keys, or replace long-lived keys with short-lived role credentials.

checks.title: Administrator permissions attached directly to a user
checks.remediation: Remove direct administrator policies and grant elevated access through roles or groups that are reviewed.

checks.title: Audit logging is not on in every region
checks.remediation: Enable a multi-region audit trail (for example AWS CloudTrail or the Azure activity log) covering all accounts.

checks.title: Audit log integrity validation is off
checks.remediation: Turn on log file integrity validation and store logs in a write-protected location.

checks.title: Audit logs are kept for less than the required period
checks.remediation: Extend log retention to at least the required period; federal guidance in OMB M-21-31 calls for longer retention for many log types.

checks.title: Cloud threat detection service is off
checks.remediation: Enable the provider's threat detection service (for example Amazon GuardDuty or Microsoft Defender for Cloud) and route alerts to your team.

checks.title: Customer-managed key rotation is off
checks.remediation: Turn on automatic yearly rotation for customer-managed keys.
